---
title: "Windows Zip and Portable Mode"
description: "Run Positron on Windows from a .zip without installing it, and use portable mode to keep settings, extensions, and logs in the same folder."
---

Every Positron release includes a `.zip` for Windows alongside the installers. The zip runs without installing anything: no registry entries, no PATH changes, and no Start menu shortcuts. Use it when you don't have permission to install software, when you want to try a version without disturbing an existing installation, or when you want Positron and all of its state to live in one folder you can move around.

Download the zip for your architecture from the [download page](download.qmd).

## Extract and run

1. Download `Positron-win32-<version>-x64.zip` (or the `arm64` zip on an ARM device).
2. Extract the whole archive to a folder you can write to, such as `C:\Users\<you>\Positron` or a folder on an external drive.
3. Run `Positron.exe` from that folder.

::: callout-important
Extract the archive fully before running it. Opening `Positron.exe` from inside the zip preview in File Explorer runs it from a temporary copy that is missing most of the application's files.
:::

A zip installation is independent of any installed copy of Positron. You can run both on the same machine.

## Portable mode

By default, the zip stores your settings, extensions, and logs in your user profile, in the same places an installed copy uses. In portable mode, it keeps them next to the application instead.

To turn on portable mode, create an empty folder named `data` next to `Positron.exe`:

```
Positron\
├── Positron.exe
├── data\
└── ...
```

The next time you start Positron, your settings, extensions, logs, and other state are written under `data\` rather than your user profile. To keep temporary files in the folder as well, create a `data\tmp` folder too.

Because everything lives in one folder, you can copy the whole folder to a USB drive or another machine and pick up where you left off.

## Updates

Positron checks for updates as usual when you run it from the zip. When a new version is available, it offers to open the download in your browser. It never installs the update for you: download the new zip, extract it, and copy your `data` folder across if you are using portable mode.

To turn the update check off, set [`update.mode`](positron://settings/update.mode) to `"none"`. See [Updating Positron](updating.qmd) for the other update settings.

## Limitations

- **Saved credentials don't travel.** Windows encrypts stored secrets, such as signed-in accounts and saved tokens, with a key tied to your Windows user account. Those secrets stay behind when you move the folder to another machine or another user account, and you will be asked to sign in again.
- **Other tools still use your user profile.** Portable mode covers Positron's own state. R, Python, Quarto, coding agents, and anything else Positron runs keep their own configuration, caches, and package libraries wherever they normally put them.
- **Portable mode is Positron's state only.** Your projects and files are wherever you saved them; the `data` folder does not move them.
